r.name: Kennet and Avon Canal Trail
r.description: Rivers linked by a canal. The name refers to the entire navigable length. From Bristol the way is the Avon. The canal is from Bath to Newbury. From there to Reading the way is the Kennet. 53 locks to Summit Pound (150 m asl) and 54 down to Reading.

Leigh Woods Veteran Tree Walk, Leigh Woods
r.description: The southern part of Leigh Woods was formerly wood pasture & is home to many veteran trees. It was historically part of the Ashton Court Estate, a SSSI to the west. These 2 sites have 1 of the largest populations of veteran trees in the South West.

r.name: Leigh Woods Woodland Wander, Leigh Woods
r.description: Pass the natural play area & walk through beautiful woodland with rare & veteran trees as well as grassland. Stokeleigh Camp hillfort is perched on the edge of the Avon Gorge, with dramatic views along the river. Some seasonally muddy / rocky sections.

r.name: Tyntesfield Woodland Walk (Long Route), Tyntesfield
r.description: This circular route takes in all aspects of the estate, including the extensive woodland. You are welcome to roam freely in the garden. This route includes unsurfaced woodland paths, steps, gravelled surfaces and steep gradients.

r.name: Tyntesfield Sidelands Walk, Tyntesfield
r.description: Discover the ancient woodlands and plantations of Tyntesfield on this gentle circular walk. In spring, the route passes carpets of bluebells in Truckle Wood & all year round there's plenty of wildlife to spot. Mostly natural surfaces & a concrete track.

r.name: Step Free Route, Tyntesfield
r.description: This route avoids steps across the estate, and loops around the house, the lower front terraces and up the Holly Walk. You are welcome to roam freely in the garden.

r.name: Watercatch Walk, Tyntesfield
r.description: This circular walk is full of historical and natural interest. Watercatch walk takes you past an old single avenue of monkey puzzle trees, a summerhouse, Watercatch and old Second World War remains, before descending into a wooded combe and back along the

r.name: Tyntesfield Tynings Walk, Tyntesfield
r.description: This gentle walk passes through ancient woodland, where there are plenty of flowers to see in the spring and meanders into a hay field full of oxeye daisies in May and June. The terrain can be uneven under foot in places and muddy when wet.

r.name: House Route, Tyntesfield
r.description: This is the shorter of the available walking routes across the estate at Tyntesfield. It loops around the house, the front terraces and up the Holly Walk, and is perfect for a relaxing stroll at any time of year.
